page.text:
A mathematical argument is far more than a sequence of assertions that
happen to be true. It is a demonstrable guarantee that a specific
conclusion is inexorably forced by accepted premises. Logic formalizes
this necessity through two fundamentally distinct, complementary
paradigms: *semantics*, which evaluates truth across abstract
mathematical structures and interpretations, and *syntax*, which governs
the mechanical derivation of symbolic formulas according to explicit
rules of inference.

The profound harmony between these two perspectives forms the foundation
of mathematical epistemology. A mature proof operates fluently across
this boundary: it harnesses structural intuition from semantics while
maintaining the uncompromising syntactic discipline that guarantees
freedom from error.
